name: South Carolina
overview: In South Carolina each county's official in charge of collecting delinquent taxes (usually the Delinquent Tax Collector or Treasurer) sells tax-delinquent real estate at a public auction at the courthouse or another convenient place in the county, after advertising it under the heading "Delinquent Tax Sale"; most counties hold one sale a year in the fall. The winning bid must be paid in full on the day of the sale by cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. The owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor, may redeem the property within twelve months from the date of the sale by paying the taxes, costs and interest on the bid amount of 3% in the first three months, 6% in months four to six, 9% in months seven to nine and 12% in the last three months, capped at the amount of the bid. If the property is not redeemed, the official makes a tax title to the purchaser.

counties.address: 301 University Ridge, Suite S-1100, Greenville, SC 29601
counties.next_sale_note: 2027 date not yet posted. The 2026 sale was October 19 - 20, 2026 at the Greenville Convention Center (past): 'October 19 - 20, 2026'.
counties.how_to_bid: Register in advance (registration opens at least 30 days before the sale; no onsite registration on sale day) using the county's online bidder registration, and bring photo ID. Bids are made in person at the public auction at the Greenville Convention Center, 1 Exposition Drive; properties are sold in alphabetical order by the defaulting taxpayer's last name, opening at the delinquent taxes, penalties and costs. The winning bid must be paid in full the day of the sale in cash, postal money order, cashier's check or certified check; failing to pay can bring a $500 per-property charge.

counties.how_to_bid: Register online through the county's tax sale bidder registration and pay the $50.00 fee by the deadline (no in-person registration). The sale is an in-person auction at the Township Auditorium; property is sold as is, for cash, to the highest bidder, with bidding opening at the delinquent taxes, costs of sale and current-year taxes. Full payment of a winning bid is required on the sale date(s) in cash, certified bank cashier's check or bank wire; bids are final and a failure to pay brings a $500.00 fine per bid plus court costs.

The property is sold for cash to the highest bidder, with immediate compliance; the starting bid includes the current year's (2026) tax.
